title: BEA distinguishes real GDP, which removes inflation, from current-dollar GDP
summary: BEA distinguishes real GDP, which removes inflation, from current-dollar GDP.
body: BEA says the figure people often call GDP is a rate of change in real GDP, and that real or chained GDP has been adjusted to remove the effects of inflation so periods can be compared. Current-dollar or nominal GDP is based on market prices during the period being measured. The source says: ""Real" or "chained" GDP numbers have been adjusted to remove the effects of inflation over time, so different periods can be compared." A rise in nominal GDP can be prices, quantities, or both. BEA's real series is the one it says has the inflation effect removed. This is a different claim from the existing card that GDP measures the value of final output.
